name: Event security and staffing

pf.license.need: The company's state security or guard license where the state requires one, and a registration for the company. Each guard holds the state's guard card where it's required. Bartenders hold a server card where the state's rules require one. A certificate of insurance (general liability, and liquor liability where bartenders pour) for any venue that asks.
pf.license.per event: Where the state's or the venue's rules require one, a permit for the event: the contract says who files it and by when.
pf.license.who holds it: The company holds its registration and insurance. Each guard and bartender holds their own card, where the state requires one.
pf.license.manager on site: A shift lead is on site at each event, and the event's own security plan is followed.
what to ask: The company's license or registration number, if the state issues one
The insurance certificate's amount and end date
Each guard's or bartender's card number and end date, if they want it shown
pf.license.how it's checked: Nothing is looked up. Rosie keeps the numbers and dates the owner gives, and the owner keeps the papers. Rosie never checks a license, card or insurance.
pf.license.blocks going live: None from Rosie: no booking is held or refused because a license can't be read. The owner decides what the company offers.
pf.license.renewals: None kept by Rosie: the owner keeps the end dates and the renewals.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance, and liquor liability for bartending; the certificate goes to any venue that asks. Rosie never verifies it.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks. Rosie never verifies them.

pf.services.online: Planning calls by video or phone.

pf.questions.who may book: An adult, a business for its event, or a venue for its client. A minor never books.

stops the booking.words: A weapon, a fight, or someone hurt at the event right now
stops the booking.says: If anyone is hurt or in danger, call 911 now and get away from it. Staff never put themselves between people and a weapon.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until it's safe; the customer can come back.

stops the booking.words: A medical emergency now (trouble breathing, a heart attack, a seizure)
stops the booking.says: Call 911 now. Staff give first aid only if they're trained to.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.words: A crowd bigger than the venue's limit
safety steps, then the booking goes on.says: The venue's limit comes first: the company can add staff only where the venue's rules allow it. The lead calls the owner.

pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, a weapon, fire, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first. Staff never use force beyond what the state's rules allow; they call 911 and the venue's security.

before the main visit.step: The staffing contract, signed on the secure page
before the main visit.timing: At booking, before any money is taken. It has the date, hours, number and kind of staff, the deposit, the cancel schedule, the rest, the venue's rules, and who files any event permit. Not signed in 24 hours: the booking is let go.
Sam sends it by 7 days before. Not sent: the venue may refuse the staff; that's the business's side.

before the main visit.step: The event permit or the venue's own rules
before the main visit.for: Where the local rules require a permit for the event or the staff
before the main visit.timing: Filed by the organizer or the company, as the contract says, by the rules' due date. Not filed: the company can't staff the event.

before the main visit.step: The final headcount and shift list
before the main visit.timing: 7 days before, on the secure page. It sets the rest. None sent: the count in the contract stands.

prep for the reminder: The staff's arrival is 30 minutes before the start, at the check-in point

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The lead gets the check-in code when the crew arrives, 30 minutes before the start. A planner or a day-of contact can get the code instead, when a mobile is given for them.
pf.visit.check-in at the kitchen: The code at the office desk for a plan meeting, or the lead types it.
pf.visit.delivery and setup: The crew arrives at the check-in point, checks in with the venue's contact, and works the posts for the hours booked.
pf.visit.food safety on the day: Staff don't serve food. A venue's food is the venue's own.
pf.visit.alcohol: Bartenders check ID for every guest who orders, and never serve anyone under 21. A guest who is visibly drunk is refused, and the lead tells the venue's contact.
pf.visit.allergies: Not part of the staffing work.
pf.visit.work changes at the event: More staff, or more hours, only with the customer's written yes by text, at the rate shown before booking. No yes in 10 minutes: the crew keeps to the booked count.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The lead texts DONE when the shift ends, with the hours worked for each person.

Small one-time shifts: paid in full when booking
Ushers and bartenders by the hour: a card saved, and the bill after the event from the hours worked

limits: Deposit cap: from the state form

pf.money.service charge: A service charge, if the contract names one, is shown before the yes. It's never called a tip.
pf.money.tips: Guests may tip staff. Tips go to the staff who worked the shift, and are never added to a bill.
pf.money.tax: Sales tax where the state's rules tax the service, from the state form.
pf.money.Rosfield's $2: Applies, as for every kind of work.

pf.messages.never in a text: Names of people to be watched for, venue codes, card details and any health detail. The shift's list stays on the secure page.

roles: Bartender (a server card where the state requires one)
skills: Plan meetings for the venue's rules
pf.staff.supervision: A shift lead is on site at each event, and the lead reports to Sam.
pf.staff.who OKs what: Sam OKs every event date, any new venue, any headcount change over 10%, and any price made for one event.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another guard or usher with the same card, if the state requires one. A lead the customer asked for by name is asked first; nobody moves on silence.
pf.staff.who does what (the example): Jo leads the events and the guards; Nico works the posts. Dana and Lou run the office and the plan meetings.

pf.rules.written contract: The staffing contract, filled in from the booking, signed by the customer and Sam before any money is taken, for every event.
pf.rules.date hold: An event date stays saved while the contract is signed: up to 24 hours here, the owner's setting.
pf.rules.events a day: The owner's own limit of events a day, by staff available.
pf.rules.final count: Due 7 days before, on the secure page. It sets the rest, charged when the shift is done. Over 10% more needs Sam's OK.
pf.rules.cancel schedule: Free to cancel for 7 days after signing. After that the deposit is kept, under the contract's dated schedule. One free date change, if staff are free that day.
pf.rules.permits: The company's own registration; an event permit where the local rules require one, filed as the contract says.
pf.rules.alcohol: Bartending only under the venue's or the company's own license, and only with each bartender's current card.
pf.rules.records: Contracts, cards, permits and payments kept 7 years, as for every kind of work. Shift lists deleted 30 days after the event.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for event staffing:
event staffing: The venue refuses the staff or the permit is not filed: the venue's rules decide, and the owner calls the customer
A guard or usher can't come: another with the same card, or a trusted stand-in if the customer agrees. A fixed-time event keeps its hours.
The crowd grows past the booked count: the lead calls the owner; more staff only with the customer's yes, at the rate shown.
A weapon or a fight: 911 first, then the lead calls the owner
A guest who is drunk or has no ID: no alcohol for them; the lead tells the venue's contact
The shift runs long: the extra hours need the customer's written yes before they're worked
The customer moves the date: one free move, if staff are free that day
Weather on the day: an outdoor event's rain or heat rule is in the contract; staff stay on site unless the venue calls it off
